text: Using a Cas9 D10A nickase with two offset sgRNAs targeting opposite strands (paired nickases) reduces off-target editing by what mechanism?
choices: It doubles the effective PAM requirement, eliminating off-target binding entirely
It shortens the guide RNA from 20 nt to 17-18 nt
A double-strand break only forms when both nicks occur near each other, so an isolated off-target single nick is simply repaired without causing a mutation
It converts Cas9 into a base editor that no longer creates any strand break
explanation: Paired nickases require two proximal, offset nicks (one per strand, from two separate sgRNA-guided sites) to generate a DSB; an off-target site would need two independent, adjacent off-target nicking events to cause damage, which is statistically rare, giving a 50- to 1500-fold reduction in off-target activity. This strategy does not eliminate the PAM requirement, it is a separate technique from guide truncation (which shortens the guide to 17-18 nt), and it is not the same mechanism as base editing.
